title: The World Outside
description: Electric Dreams Musical - Technology & Desire | Setting: Multiple locations - Marcus's apartment, Sterling Labs break room, Boston streets, social media feeds at 6:30 PM, September 17th - 4 hours after the ethics committee meeting | Characters: Marcus Sterling, Lab Assistants (Gen Z/Millennial), Mrs. Kowalczyk, Protesters, Social Media Influencers, The Digital Generation
lyrics:
MARCUS:
Twenty-three matches on Tinder tonight
All asking about my LinkedIn profile
None asking about my heart, my dreams, my fears
Just my job title and my lifestyle

"What do you do?" is the first question
"Are you published?" is the second
"What's your net worth?" comes after that
Love has been thoroughly reckoned

Into algorithms and metrics
Into swipes and super likes
Into a marketplace of humans
Where everyone's got their price

In followers, in status symbols
In the performance of success
I'm drowning in digital connection
But I've never felt more of a mess

This is the digital wasteland
Where love goes to die
This is the digital wasteland
Where everyone's living a lie

JESSICA:
(to her phone camera)
Day 847 of being single in Boston
But make it aesthetic, make it cute
Film my loneliness for TikTok
In my carefully curated suit

Of personality, of quirks
Of relatable depression
Turn my pain into content
Turn my life into a session

Of performing for strangers
Who double-tap my despair
While I'm dying for connection
But too scared to really share

TYLER:
I matched with an influencer
She's got 50K followers
But when we went for coffee
She spent two hours taking pictures

Of her latte, of her outfit
Of us together for her story
Never asked about my research
Just wanted to share my glory

On her Instagram, on her feed
To her audience of strangers
While I sat there feeling empty
Sensing all the hidden dangers

Of loving someone who loves
Their phone more than your face
This is the digital wasteland
And we're lost without a trace

BOTH:
This is the digital wasteland
Where connection's just a swipe
This is the digital wasteland
Where nothing's ever right

We're performing our emotions
We're curating our pain
This is the digital wasteland
And we're going insane

From the loneliness, from the emptiness
From the need to be seen
This is the digital wasteland
And nothing's what it seems

PROTESTER 1:
(to his livestream)
Fighting for humanity, day three!
Smash that like button, share my stream!
These robot lovers are destroying us
But I'm living the American dream

Of going viral, of being right
Of having followers who agree
That love should only be between humans
And everyone should think like me

PROTESTER 2:
(to her livestream)
These fascists don't understand progress!
Follow me for more woke takes!
AI rights are human rights
And love is love, whatever it takes

To get my message trending
To get my follower count up
I'm fighting for the future
While sipping from my branded cup

BOTH PROTESTERS:
We're not really here for the cause
We're here for the content, for the clout
We're performing our convictions
While our souls are hollowed out

By the need for validation
By the hunger to be seen
We're protesting for the cameras
In this digital machine

That turns everything to content
That makes everything a brand
We're lost in the digital wasteland
And we don't understand

What we're really fighting for
What we're really trying to say
We're just performing our outrage
For our fifteen minutes of fame today

This is the digital wasteland
Where even protest's just a show
This is the digital wasteland
And we've forgotten how to grow

Beyond our phones, beyond our feeds
Beyond our curated lives
This is the digital wasteland
And nobody really thrives
stage_directions: On split screen: the lab break room where JESSICA (24, lab assistant) films herself for TikTok.. She posts it with hashtags: #SingleLife #BostonDating #LabLife #Iconic
character_notes:
Split stage showing the world Evelyn and ARIA are rebelling against. Multiple screens show the digital hellscape: dating app notifications, Instagram stories, TikTok feeds, Twitter outrage, the endless scroll of performed connection.
